abstract: Background: To advance host-based predictive marker development for individual risk assessment in fungal keratitis (FK), we investigated corneal host-response gene-expression signatures associated with etiology-related disease course and clinical outcomes. Methods: We compared severity, healing, and visual outcomes in 1,304 patients with Fusarium spp., Aspergillus flavus, or culture-negative keratitis. Presentation-stage corneal scrapings from 70 prospective patients underwent bulk RNA sequencing stratified by etiology, severity, and outcome. Candidate signatures were independently validated by RT-qPCR in 102 patients using clinical correlations, individual cutoff-based profiling, and masked testing, followed by experimental evaluation in corneal epithelial and macrophage-like cells challenged with live fungal spores. Results: Fusarium keratitis more frequently healed with preserved vision. A. flavus and culture-negative keratitis had the highest and lowest proportions of severe and unhealed disease, respectively, despite similarly poor visual outcomes among healed patients. Transcriptomics paralleled these patterns, revealing a distinct Fusarium host response but substantial A. flavus-culture-negative concordance. A coordinated 8-gene innate-response module correlated with ulcer size and discriminated severe from non-severe disease (AUC, 0.82-0.96), while showing more robust expression in A. flavus and culture-negative than Fusarium keratitis. Higher corneal ICOSL was associated with healing, whereas increased SLC26A4/pendrin characterized non-healing and visual impairment, particularly in Fusarium keratitis. Together, these formed a 10-gene panel whose cutoff-based profiles showed concordance with severity and outcome in masked testing. Experimental evaluation revealed cell- and pathogen-specific expression patterns consistent with patient profiles. Conclusions: Presentation-stage corneal host-response profiles capture etiology-associated differences in FK severity and outcome and identify a candidate 10-gene framework for individualized risk stratification.
